q: Chemistry is after all the study of all , its composition, its properties, and its transformation from one form to another.
e: Chemistry is after all the study of all, its composition, its properties, and its transformation from one form to another. Chemistry studies matter and the changes matter undergoes.

q: Matter is made up of ____ particles.
e: Matter is made up of tiny particles. Tiny is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These can be atoms or ____ (groups of atoms), and elements or compounds.
e: These can be atoms or molecules (groups of atoms), and elements or compounds. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The air (gas), the sea water (liquid), and alloys (solid) are not pure substances; they are ____.
e: The air (gas), the sea water (liquid), and alloys (solid) are not pure substances; they are mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: Different methods of separation depend on whether the substances to be separated are solids, liquids or ____.
e: Different methods of separation depend on whether the substances to be separated are solids, liquids or gases. Gases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The most common states of matter are solid, liquid and ____.
e: The most common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas. Gas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The properties of each state of matter depend on the forces of attraction between the particles which can be weak or ____.
e: The properties of each state of matter depend on the forces of attraction between the particles which can be weak or strong. Strong is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one ____.
e: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one another. Another is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solids have a definite shape and ____.
e: Solids have a definite shape and volume. Volume is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Liquids are composed of particles which are not fixed in any definite positions as in the ____.
e: Liquids are composed of particles which are not fixed in any definite positions as in the solids. In a solid, particles are packed tightly with strong forces, so the shape is fixed.

q: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in ____.
e: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in gases. Gases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between ____ particles.
e: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between gaseous particles. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hence, gases do not have a definite volume and shape of their ____.
e: Hence, gases do not have a definite volume and shape of their own. Own is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It can be clearly visible in particles of smoke suspended in a gas because of the effect known as ____ motion.
e: It can be clearly visible in particles of smoke suspended in a gas because of the effect known as Brownian motion. Brownian motion is the random jiggling of tiny particles hit by fast molecules in a fluid.

q: Diffusion can be explained by the ____ motion.
e: Diffusion can be explained by the Brownian motion. Brownian motion is the random jiggling of tiny particles hit by fast molecules in a fluid.

q: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of ____ substance.
e: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of another substance. Another is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and ____.
e: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and gases. Gases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the ____.
e: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles ____.
e: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles diffuse. Diffuse is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse ____.
e: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse faster. Faster is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from collisions with the gas or liquid ____.
e: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from collisions with the gas or liquid particles. In a liquid, particles touch but can slide, so volume is fixed while shape is not. In a gas, particles are far apart, move fast, and have weak attractions.
